headline: Israeli Gaza documentary wins in Venice, angers Israel

sources.title: An Israeli documentary on the war in Gaza sets off a firestorm at home after Venice award (AP via KIRO 7)
NAZA documentary about IDF tactics in Gaza prompts 'treason' accusations in Israel (ABC News Australia)
Israel probing Naza film on Gaza for treason, inciting anti-Semitism (Al Jazeera)
New documentary on Israel killing civilians in Gaza won global plaudits. But it's facing intense backlash at home. (NBC News)

chunks.text: An Israeli documentary about the war in Gaza has {{set off}} a fierce argument at home. The film, titled Naza, {{walked away with}} the [[special jury prize]] at the Venice Film Festival on September 12, 2026. Its two directors won an Oscar in 2025 for an earlier film. The title comes from a Hebrew military term for [[collateral damage]]. After the Venice screening, the audience {{carried on}} applauding for 25 minutes.

verbs.correct: To cause something to start suddenly
verbs.wrong: To move an event to a later date
verbs.why: A small comment can set off a long argument, and one news report can set off a wave of complaints. The prize in Venice set off a fierce argument in Israel about the film.

verbs.correct: To win something easily or clearly
verbs.wrong: To leave a place without paying
verbs.why: Our team walked away with the trophy again this year, and the young singer walked away with the top prize. Naza walked away with the special jury prize at the Venice Film Festival.

verbs.wrong: To pass news to another person
verbs.why: The teacher carried on talking after the bell, and the workers carried on despite the rain. The audience in Venice carried on applauding the film for 25 minutes.

chunks.text: The film {{draws on}} [[testimony]] from 24 military [[insiders]], including [[intelligence officers]] and soldiers, who speak [[anonymously]]. They say Israel used [[artificial intelligence]] to {{pick out}} targets in Gaza, often knowing that many civilians would likely die. The Israeli military acknowledges using AI to help identify targets, but says a human makes the final decision before any [[strike]]. The film has not {{come out}} anywhere yet. The directors plan to seek [[distribution]] in Israel, Europe and the US.

verbs.correct: To use something as a source
verbs.why: A good novel draws on the writer's own life, and a report often draws on interviews with workers. The film draws on testimony from 24 military insiders.

verbs.correct: To choose one thing from a group
verbs.wrong: To find fault with someone's work
verbs.why: She picked out a blue dress for the wedding, and the coach picked out two players for the final. The soldiers say AI was used to pick out targets in Gaza.

verbs.correct: To become available to the public
verbs.wrong: To be proven true in the end
verbs.why: The new phone comes out in October, and her second album came out last spring. Naza has not come out anywhere yet, and the directors are still seeking distribution.

chunks.text: Israel's leaders {{hit back}} quickly. The prime minister accused the filmmakers of [[incitement]] and antisemitism. The head of the Israeli military ordered military prosecutors to {{look into}} possible [[leaks]] of [[classified material]] and to consider [[criminal charges]]. The culture minister asked the interior ministry to consider {{taking away}} the directors' [[citizenship]]. Several of these officials admitted they had not seen the film. Dozens of [[protesters]] {{turned up}} outside the home of one director's parents.

verbs.correct: To answer an attack with your own attack
verbs.wrong: To return home after a long journey
verbs.why: The mayor hit back at critics in a radio interview, and the company hit back with a statement of its own. Israel's leaders hit back quickly after the film won in Venice.

verbs.correct: To examine a matter to learn the facts
verbs.wrong: To watch something closely from far away
verbs.why: The police are looking into the missing money, and the school promised to look into the complaint. Military prosecutors were told to look into possible leaks of classified material.

verbs.wrong: To hold someone at a police station
verbs.why: The referee took away the goal, and the court took away his driver's license. The culture minister asked the interior ministry to consider taking away the directors' citizenship.
Hundreds of fans turned up at the airport, and my cousin turned up late to the party. Dozens of protesters turned up outside the home of one director's parents.

chunks.text: The directors {{stand by}} the film. One director said many soldiers had been waiting for a chance to talk. Co-producer The Guardian said the testimonies are true. A [[press freedom]] group {{spoke out}} against the prime minister's threats. Most Israelis see the war as [[self-defense]] after the attack of October 7, 2023, while abroad it has drawn accusations of [[war crimes]]. Naza screens at the New York Film Festival later this month, so the argument will not {{die down}} soon.

verbs.correct: To keep supporting a decision or claim
verbs.wrong: To take the place of someone absent
verbs.why: The doctor stood by her advice after the review, and the coach stands by his decision to change the team. The directors stand by the film despite the attacks from officials.

verbs.correct: To say your opinion publicly and openly
verbs.wrong: To read a text aloud to a room
verbs.why: Parents spoke out against the school closure, and some players have spoken out about unfair pay. A press freedom group spoke out against the prime minister's threats.

verbs.wrong: To stop working for a short break
verbs.why: The wind died down by the evening, and the laughter died down when the teacher walked in. With a New York screening coming, the argument over Naza will not die down soon.

mainIdea.s: A film where unnamed soldiers describe how Gaza targets were chosen won a prize in Venice. Israeli leaders answered with talk of charges and lost citizenship, and its directors stand by it.
mainIdea.why: The prize set off threats of prosecution and citizenship loss, while the directors and the co-producer defend the testimonies as true.

mainIdea.s: A film about the war in Gaza won a prize in Venice after the Israeli military screened it for its own soldiers. Officials now say the film was leaked without the army's permission.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the military did not screen the film. Officials admitted they had not seen it, and the film has not come out anywhere yet.

mainIdea.s: Two Israeli directors were stopped at the airport on their way to a film festival in Venice. Their documentary about the war in Gaza was then pulled from the program by a court order.
mainIdea.why: The film was shown in Venice and won the special jury prize. Nobody was stopped at an airport and no court pulled it from the program.

tf.s: Naza walked away with the special jury prize in Venice on September 12, 2026.
